the biden administration was confident a tough sanctions regime would bring the russians to their knees. 

four years later…they’re still fighting a brutal war against ukraine.

whose political leadership is more vulnerable to sustained economic damage, the united states or the islamic republic?

president trump is convinced it’s the iranians. he has very little information supporting that view.
that’s a very exciting / dramatic post. as for me, what’s essential is that i tell people my honest assessment.
it’s plausible powell wants to stay at the fed purely to annoy trump

what would the poem on the statue of liberty say if it were written today?

not “give me your tired, your poor” but maybe “give me your millionaires and your social media history”

with @trevornoah

Video

during the 1973 oil crisis, private companies controlled 85% of global proven reserves. 

today, state owned enterprises control 75%. (and that number would be 90% if it wasn’t for the shale boom)

this isn’t just about oil.
it’s about two competing visions
for the middle east.
and they’re starting to clash.
@gzeromedia

Video

the iran war is the first time of trump’s presidency—in either term—that he is responsible for a major economic downturn. 

i don’t see any capacity (and, for now, even any intent) to turn this around before midterm elections in november.
moose has no problem with stairs. but that doesn’t mean he climbs them unnecessarily.
king charles bringing the most deft diplomacy—by a long margin—that we’ve seen visiting the trump administration this term.
it was embarrassing and tacky when biden put his face on the us passport. it’s embarrassing and tacky when trump does it.

gulf unity is cracking.
the gcc could be next.
what held the region together
isn’t holding anymore.
@gzeromedia

Video

uae is withdrawing from opec. 
what looks like energy politics is something deeper.
a fight over the region’s future.
